name: Preparation H under eyes

card.summary: Hemorrhoid cream dabbed under the eyes on the theory that its vasoconstrictor shrinks bags; no studies support or test the practice.
card.note: Off-label; some formulations contain hydrocortisone and the product is not made for eyelids.

quick.overview:
Some people apply Preparation H, a hemorrhoid treatment, to the skin under the eyes, reasoning that its blood-vessel constrictor will reduce puffiness. The idea circulates as a beauty hack.

No clinical study of this use was found, and the product is labelled for hemorrhoids.
quick.mechanism: Some versions contain 0.25% phenylephrine, a vasoconstrictor, and shark liver oil; others use 1% hydrocortisone or other actives. Proponents say vasoconstriction shrinks swelling. Formulations differ by country.
quick.risks: The product is made for anorectal use, not eyelids. Dermatology references note that vasoconstrictors can be followed by rebound darkening, and steroid versions raise skin-thinning concerns. No safety data for periorbital use were found.

lead: Preparation H under eyes is an off-label practice in which the hemorrhoid product Preparation H is applied to the skin beneath the eyes, in the belief that it reduces puffiness and bags.

Preparation H is an American brand now owned by Pfizer, sold as gels, ointments, suppositories and wipes; active ingredients vary by country and include phenylephrine, hydrocortisone, pramoxine, witch hazel and caffeine, and some versions contain shark liver oil or yeast extract.[1] Proponents point to the phenylephrine, a blood-vessel constrictor, as the active mechanism.[1]

No study of the product on periorbital skin was found. The only related published work found concerns wound healing in the rectum.[3] Reference material on dark circles notes that medications causing rebound after vasoconstrictors can darken the area.[2]

paras: The original formulation was developed by inventor George Sperti with a yeast extract as the main ingredient; the manufacturer's predecessor acquired the product in the 1930s and it became a leading hemorrhoid treatment.[1] A yeast extract component was removed from the US formulation in 1995 but remained in the Canadian one.[1]

Believers say phenylephrine constricts the small vessels beneath thin eyelid skin and reduces swelling. Whether the product has that effect on the periorbital area has not been tested. Dermatology references describe rebound vasodilation after vasoconstrictors as a possible cause of darkened skin.[2]
The product is labelled for anorectal use. Formulations containing hydrocortisone are corticosteroids, and eyelid skin is thin; no data were found for this use.
No studies found for use under the eyes. A 1984 study examined the product's effect on wound healing in the human rectum, which does not address appearance.[3]

timeline.event: American Home Products acquires a sunburn oil later developed into Preparation H.[1]
Yeast extract removed from the US formulation.[1]
Pfizer acquires Wyeth, the brand's owner.[1]
